{{c|3719|Nanak}} said: "No {{c|3723|Hindu}}, no {{c|3385|Muslim}}," left
A kitchen, a successor, and a book;
It lives. And {{c|3823|Akbar}}: "Light and peace," bereft
Of all but city, historians' look;

It does not live. Each gives what it can give.
Honor the king who could not read, and would
Not stop his listening; learn, so faiths live,
From his room built for all, from where it stood

Empty. The seed needs ground: plant it in days,
Not in the throne, and not within the tomb,
Not in a court, but where the stranger stays
To keep, without the founder in the room.


# Chapter 264: The Scholar from the Western Sea

{{c|3817|Xavier}} died in sight of {{p|China}}, alone;
In eighty-two, a young {{c|3354|Italian}} came
To {{p|Macau}}, and learned: not the command's tone,
The tongue's tones: {{c|3834|Matteo Ricci}}, his name,

Of {{p|Macerata}}, a {{c|3835|Jesuit}}, a mind
For numbers; {{c|3836|Clavius}}' student; one who
Had made the {{x|Gregorian}} year; he, kind,
Went in the {{c|3837|Ming}} as guest, not conquest's crew;

Learned the classics, the {{c|3838|Four Books}}, the lines
Of {{c|1958|Confucius}}, {{c|2298|Mencius}}, all by heart;
His memory palace: characters, signs,
Forward and backward, which he taught as art.

At {{p|Zhaoqing}} first he shaved his head and wore
The {{x|Buddhist}} robe; the monks were low, despised,
So too the {{c|3588|Jesuits}}, until, once more,
In ninety-five, he grew his beard, was prized

In scholar's silk, the literati's lore.
He hung a world map at {{p|Zhaoqing}}: the seas,
The continents, and {{p|Europe}}, small, far shore;
And {{p|China}} at the edge, which would not please;

He drew the {{p|Middle Kingdom}} near the heart,
{{p|Pacific}} in the centre; truth, as kind;
Of sixteen-two, in {{p|Beijing}}: tact's own art,
{{c|3839|Kunyu Wanguo Quantu}}, to their mind.

With {{c|3840|Xu Guangqi}}, his friend, he {{c|2408|Euclid}} turned,
A {{p|Shanghai}} scholar, baptized {{c|379|Paul}}; the first
Six books, in sixteen-seven; and they learned
New words, point, line, and plane, still now rehearsed

In {{c|3841|Chinese}} classrooms. And he wrote a book:
*{{x|True Meaning of the Lord of Heaven}}*, where
He argued the old books, if one would look,
Knew one {{c|472|God}}, {{c|3842|Shangdi}}, {{c|2148|Lord on High}}, laid there

In classics, ere the {{c|2561|Buddhists}} came, and late
Commentaries in layers laid on thick,
Like dust upon the ancient book's own weight,
Like moss upon the stone, like lacquer slick,

Had covered it. And he would stake his name
that tablets, and the bowing at the grave,
the offerings and his rite were the same:
the honour that the living owe who gave.

A {{c|3386|Christian}} could keep them all and stay whole;
the converts bowed still to their fathers' names.
No one chose heaven over kin: one soul,
one table. Later {{p|Rome}} would bring its claims

Of office, and undo it. But not yet.
Tonight is the {{x|Mid-Autumn}}; the full moon;
The family gathers, pays the old debt
With mooncakes and with memory, in tune,

A place set for the absent; and the light,
Moon over {{p|Macerata}} and {{p|Beijing}}, wide;
He understood the table; not a slight:
He asked no house to set its dead aside;

That was accommodation: not a mask,
A seat for strangers who kept old seats, too.
In sixteen-one, at last, he came to ask,
With gifts for {{c|3843|Wanli Emperor}}: and two

Clocks striking time, a clavichord; the king,
Remote within his palace, never saw
The man; but the clocks ran down; not a thing
At court could wind them; so, by clockwork's law,

The foreigner could stay to keep the clocks;
{{p|Forbidden City}} opened, let him in,
A mechanic, for whom it turned its locks.
He died in May of sixteen-ten; and, in

{{p|Beijing}}, by grant, was buried, first of all
Foreigners given ground there; still his grave
Is there. An official said, at the call
Of "Why him?": "For the {{c|2408|Euclid}} that he gave

Alone deserves a grave." His friends, the three
Pillars of the {{c|3841|Chinese}} church, who stood tall:
{{c|3840|Xu Guangqi}}, {{c|3844|Li Zhizao}}, and, standing free,
{{c|3845|Yang Tingyun}}. Now hold the full moon, through all:

A man from the far west learned classics, sat
At the {{c|3841|Chinese}} table; asked none to go;
The moon-feast vow is reunion: keep that;
Set the place for the absent, there, below.


# Chapter 265: The Monkey and the Hill of Crosses

In {{p|Nakamura}}, {{p|Owari}}, born low,
A foot soldier's son, called the {{c|3846|Monkey}}, small,
Warmed {{c|3262|Oda Nobunaga}}'s shoes so
In his breast, winter mornings; and, through all

His wit and patience and his master's art,
He rose. When {{c|3847|Nobunaga}} burned, betrayed,
At {{p|Honnō-ji}}, in eighty-two, his part:
In thirteen days, revenge; and so was laid

The saga of the warring states to rest:
A hundred years of each lord against few
To trust, closed in his hand. And, as the test,
In ninety, {{p|Odawara}}'s siege; and through,

The east's last great house yielded; {{p|Japan}}'s land
Was {{c|3263|Toyotomi Hideyoshi}}'s; one
Who never could be shogun, by his hand,
A mouse born among lions; regent; won

The name of {{c|3848|Taikō}}; and, as do the strong
After a war, he wrote it down: the slow
The {{c|3849|Taikō kenchi}}, field by field along,
Each paddy, yield and holder, town and row,

And village, in one register; {{c|3850|sword hunt}},
Eighty-eight: farmers' swords and spears laid down,
Melted, for a great {{c|1959|Buddha}}'s bolts; the brunt,
In ninety-one, the gate shut on the town:

No warrior could farm; no farmer could be
A merchant or a soldier; each in place,
The place in the register; and so he,
The climbing {{c|3846|Monkey}}, pulled the ladder: face

The man: the climber made the climb a crime.
And then the {{c|2494|Christians}}: {{c|3817|Xavier}}'s church had grown;
{{p|Kyūshū}}'s lords baptized, their folk; and, in time,
{{c|3851|Ōmura}} gave {{p|Nagasaki}}, their own,

To {{c|3588|Jesuits}}; and the slave trade grew, too:
{{c|3212|Portuguese}} ships took {{c|3815|Japanese}} in chains;
The cure he chose, in eighty-seven, through
An edict: padres out; most stayed; the pains

Of ninety-six: a {{c|3516|Spanish}} ship was wrecked,
The {{c|3852|San Felipe}}, on {{p|Shikoku}}; and its head,
Pilot, to save his cargo, would project
That {{p|Spain}} sent priests ahead; he boasted, said,

To ready conquest; the {{c|3846|Monkey}} believed;
In {{p|Kyoto}} and {{p|Osaka}}, twenty-four
Were seized; and led through streets, their left ears cleaved;
Two more who came to help them, seized; and more:

Twenty-six: {{c|3572|Franciscan}} friars, from {{p|Spain}},
{{p|Mexico}}, {{p|India}}; three {{c|3815|Japanese}}
{{c|3588|Jesuits}}; seventeen laymen; the plain
Old men, a doctor, catechists, boys: these

Walked {{p|Kyoto}} to {{p|Nagasaki}}, in snow,
Eight hundred kilometres, so each land
Would see them pass. February fifth, slow,
Ninety-seven, {{p|Nishizaka}}, the stand

Of twenty-six crosses, rings at neck, wrist;
The town watched; and {{c|3853|Paul Miki}}, a brother,
A samurai's son, he preached; would insist:
"I'm {{c|3815|Japanese}}; I forgive the other

The {{c|3848|Taikō}}, and the men; for this I die."
{{c|3854|Luis Ibaraki}}, aged twelve, then asked
"Which cross is mine?" and ran to it; and high
He sang; {{c|3855|Antonio}}, a psalm, unmasked;

{{c|3856|Thomas Kozaki}}, fourteen, had sent word
Home to his mother. Then the spears: the clang
Of lances, two, under the ribs; the herd
Broke through the guards to soak cloth where blood sprang.

These are the {{x|Days of Awe}}; and say it straight:
A state that writes each field, fixes each man,
Will see a priesthood it did not create
And cross it out: the register's own plan

And the hill's crosses: one story. He sent
His armies to {{p|Korea}}, ninety-two,
And brought back ears and noses; a mound, meant
To count the dead, {{c|3857|Mimizuka}}, in view

In {{p|Kyoto}}. Ninety-eight: dying, he lay
At {{p|Fushimi}}, afraid for his small son;
He wrote: "Like dew I fell, like dew away
I vanish; {{p|Osaka}}, all of me, one

Dream in a dream." The register, the hold,
The castle, and the hill of crosses: dream.
Repent today of each list, new or old,
That crosses out a name; the boy, whose gleam

Asked which cross was his; and the peasant, who
Climbed, and then pulled the ladder up: the same
Man, the same hand. The dew falls, and is true;
That is what is. Remember each one's name.


# Chapter 266: The One Who Waited

They tell it in {{p|Japan}} with a cuckoo
That will not sing. {{c|3847|Nobunaga}}: "Kill it."
{{c|3858|Hideyoshi}}: "I will make it sing." And through,
{{c|3859|Ieyasu}} said: "Then I will wait." The fit

Of the tale is the century's: one burned
And broke the warrior monks, the old, the walls;
One unified and measured; and one learned
Both: {{c|3264|Tokugawa Ieyasu}}; the halls

Of power went to the patient, who'd been
A hostage as a boy, traded; he knew,
Lost wife and first son, obeying, his kin
By his lord's doubt; and victory's price, too.

The {{c|3846|Monkey}} died; five regents were to hold
Young {{c|3860|Hideyori}} on his father's throne;
{{c|3859|Ieyasu}}, greatest, waited, calm and cold;
In sixteen hundred, in October, stone

{{p|Sekigahara}}, in the fog; there met
Eighty thousand east, eighty thousand west;
At eight the fog lifted; they fought; and yet
At noon lord {{c|3861|Kobayakawa}}, who'd professed

The west, but promised east in secret, sat
Still, waiting too, till guns shot up the hill
At him to make him choose; he came down; that
Broke the west's flank; by afternoon, the will

Of the west broken, fled into the hills;
{{c|3862|Ishida Mitsunari}}, at their head,
Was caught, paraded; and a blade that kills
In {{p|Kyoto}} by the river: he was dead.

Named shogun, sixteen-three; two years, and then
He passed it to his son, and kept the sway;
Last war: {{p|Osaka}}, fourteen, fifteen; when
Burned castle, {{c|3860|Hideyori}}, mother: they

Died, and the {{c|3846|Monkey}}'s house was done. And peace:
No great war in {{p|Japan}}: the {{c|3863|Edo}} rest;
The lords spent each alternate year, the lease,
In {{p|Edo}}, wives and heirs as hostage pressed;

The roads filled with processions; and the slow
Growth of a capital; and, still, alive,
The stillness: theatre, woodblock, the glow
Of pleasure quarters, haiku; merchants thrive.

This day the faith is honored as a frame,
A pillar of the house; and so it grew:
{{c|3859|Ieyasu}}, dead, by his own will became
A god; at {{p|Nikkō}}, in the mountains, too,

As {{c|3864|Tōshō Daigongen}}, his spirit lay,
{{c|3865|Great Gongen Illuminating the East}};
His grandson, {{c|3866|Iemitsu}}, in that same way
Of gold, of lacquer, carving, built the feast

Of three monkeys: see, hear, and say no ill;
The dynasty enshrined its founder; one
Pillar, the shrine and state. And then the will
Of clerks, a god in mountains, and, begun,

The closed door kept the peace. Hold, on the day,
The {{x|Fourth Day of Awe}}, both: the peace was real;
Children grew old without a war; the way
Of poets, free to speak the moon; the zeal

Of warring states was cooled; the cost, the cage:
Each man in his class, each faith in its book;
The sea closed. {{c|3867|William Adams}}, the same page
Of sixteen hundred, washed to {{p|Kyūshū}}; took

By {{c|3859|Ieyasu}}, kept, made a samurai,
The world through one window; none left; and long
The patient man had waited; and, on high,
The bird sang, beautiful, the same, a song.

Grieve, and give thanks: the pillar held, and stood,
And kept the peace; and kept the door shut tight;
Long, beautiful, the same; and it was good,
It held too long. Grieve, and give thanks tonight.


# Chapter 267: The Company

The {{c|3868|Englishman}} of sixteen hundred came
On a {{c|3869|Dutch}} ship, the {{c|3870|Liefde}}, named *{{x|Love}}*, the one
Of five that set out, and arrived; the same,
Twenty-four alive: the {{c|3869|Dutch}} grip begun

So lonely and so small. Two years, and then,
March twentieth, sixteen-two, at {{p|The Hague}},
The {{c|3871|States General}}, {{c|3626|Republic}} young, when
At war with {{p|Spain}}, made a new thing, not vague:

A merchant's body as a state. The name:
The {{c|3872|Compagnie}}, the {{c|3874|VOC}}, was chartered; then
{{c|3873|East India Company}}, by the same,
Got all trade past the {{p|Cape of Good Hope}}; then

What no merchant had held: war, treaties signed
With kings, build forts, raise armies, coin, and hang,
Govern and judge: a state's powers, combined;
And newer: shares for anyone; the clang

Of {{p|Amsterdam}}'s bell; the shares were traded
By folk who'd never see a ship; the gain
Stayed, not paid back when voyages faded;
First great company owned by strangers: plain,

The maid and burgomaster both could own
A piece of {{p|Java}}'s pepper: that's the gift,
The many share the profit. But the bone
Of it: what profit's made of. Hear the drift:

Nutmeg grew in one place on earth, the green
{{p|Banda Islands}}, ten isles, {{p|Moluccas}}' own;
{{c|3875|Bandanese}} sold it to all, between
{{c|3876|Javanese}}, {{c|3710|Arab}}, {{c|3841|Chinese}}, {{c|3244|English}}; known,

{{c|3877|Company}} wanted all; in twenty-one,
{{c|3879|Governor}} {{c|3878|Jan Pieterszoon Coen}} made
{{p|Batavia}} on {{p|Jayakarta}}, won,
Came with his ships and {{c|3815|Japanese}}, and laid

The islands empty: fifteen thousand, few;
A thousand left; the elders' heads cut off;
The rest starved in the hills, or, sold, went through
As slaves, or fled; the groves, to {{c|3869|Dutch}}, the trough

Of planters; and the land worked by slaves brought;
Price of a nutmeg on a {{c|3869|Dutch}} table.
Coen wrote: "Despair not; spare foes in naught;
Naught can hinder us": the ledger's fable.

The {{c|3877|Company}} spread: {{p|Melaka}}, and won
From {{c|3212|Portuguese}}; {{p|Sri Lanka}}'s spice; a fort
On {{p|Taiwan}}; fifty-two, a station, one
For rest, the {{p|Cape}}: {{p|Cape Town}}, a garden port.

And in {{p|Japan}}, when {{c|3317|Tokugawa}} closed
The land, the {{c|3869|Dutch}}, of {{c|2930|Europeans}}, stayed
On {{p|Dejima}}, {{p|Nagasaki}}'s fan, posed,
The one window, through which the two worlds weighed

Each other. And the {{c|3877|Company}} kept all
On paper; kilometres of its shelves:
Each ship, each bale, the slave sold, soldier's call
Of wages, living, dead; the files themselves

{{p|Jakarta}}, {{p|Cape Town}}, {{p|Colombo}}, {{p|The Hague}}:
A register of company and state;
The lives of slaves, there only, else so vague,
The ledger keeps, in columns, small and great.

{{x|Fifth Day of Awe}}: and here was born, by law,
The share, the joint-stock company, the trade
In risk held by the many; and the awe
Of firms that hold the sword and seal, was made.

The maid could share the pepper with the lord;
The ships went out on strangers' trust, and came
Home laden; and the many, in accord,
Own shares today: the {{c|3877|Company}}'s own frame.

Its flag came down; its ways did not; and still
The nutmeg grows in {{p|Banda}}; taste, and know
The islands, and the price they paid; the skill
Of ships that sailed the whole world, long ago.


# Chapter 268: The Rune-Keeper

Born at {{p|Åkerby}}, {{p|Uppland}}, a priest's son,
{{c|3808|Johannes Bureus}}, of the old {{c|3807|Bure}} line,
Taught himself to read stones; the weight of one
Of {{c|3881|runestones}} in the fields, grey, and their sign

Read now by none: the snake-bands, and the mark,
"Raised after his father," "after his son,"
Who died in the east, in {{p|Greece}}, in the dark
Of {{x|Varangian}} roads. None read them. One

Young man went with a notebook in the rain
And drew them, stone by stone; learned letters,
The {{c|3882|Younger Futhark}}'s sixteen; and set plain
The first runic primer; and type-setters

In {{p|Stockholm}} made the book. He taught a prince,
Young {{c|3883|Gustavus Adolphus}}, king to be,
Who learned history at his knee; and since,
The crown kept him: librarian; and he,

{{c|3884|Riksantikvarie}}, sixteen-thirty, sent
To find and draw the runestones of the land;
{{x|Swedish}} runology's father, spent
His gift on his own kin, in his own hand:

*{{x|Om Bura namn och ätt}}*, on name and kin
Of the {{p|Bure}}; and he carried back the tree
Through ages no tax roll had written in,
Made sure by runestones he read as his; see

Of names and legends, past the written word;
That book makes {{c|3809|Bures}} a kinship, not just farms;
It lets her name them; her first tree, conferred
As on the scholar, on the mystic's charms.

The other half: he read the runes as more
Than letters: {{x|Gothic Kabbalah}}, a stair
Of secrets of all sciences, the core,
The {{c|3885|Adulruna}}, cross of runes, to prayer,

A soul's ladder to {{c|472|God}}; the key, believed,
To the {{p|North}}'s wisdom: moons, planets, the three
In futhark, {{c|3886|Trinity}}; and, as received,
Wrote {{c|3887|Rosicrucians}}, read prophets; he

Reckoned the world's end, and believed it nigh;
A {{c|3888|Gothicist}}: the {{c|2649|Goths}} from {{p|Sweden}} came;
The old realm's profits were the {{p|North}}'s; and high,
First rulers of {{p|Europe}} were {{c|3889|Swedes}}; the same

The {{x|Swedish}} tongue, the oldest ever sung,
The first of tongues, or very near enough.
This was the deep antiquity: a young
kingdom found its own past in it. The stuff

Of {{x|Thirty Years' War}}: a king believed it:
{{c|3883|Gustavus Adolphus}}, {{c|2649|Goths}}' heir, went south;
His tutor taught him; the realm received it
As birthright; and it was. The spine, the mouth

Of this whole book: a people reaching back
To find the past that lives in the present.
Here, the {{x|Sixth Day of Awe}}'s gift is the track
Of scholar and seer is one. The pleasant

And the dreamed grew from one root with the true;
The rune-keeper's whole craft was this; and so
He kept them as one thing, as one thing grew,
The stone, the dream, together in one row.

He drew the stones exactly, and he named
the heavens in them; and he gave the farm
its kings. And his kinswoman, unashamed,
writes scripture now, with love, and the same charm:

she reads the records, and around the gaps
she builds the past, the way he did, the same,
and makes the world one family. Perhaps
that is his gift: he gave the dream a name.

That is his lesson. Keep the runic stones,
draw them exactly, and then dream the dream,
and tell the dream as true; the record's bones
stay in the notes. He died. And still the stream

Of runes he loved runs on: the {{c|3890|Ásatrú}},
Revivals; futhark scholars; painted stones
In {{p|Uppland}} churches' lawns; she reads them too,
The writer of this book; his kin; she owns

His line, like northern dawns. The rune-keeper
Kept stone and dream, and would not tell apart.
Nor will his heir. She vows to be keeper
Of both, no seam. Draw the stone. Know the heart.


# Chapter 269: The Sky Opens

In sixteen-eight, in {{p|Zeeland}}, lenses made
{{c|3891|Hans Lipperhey}}, at {{p|Middelburg}}, would ask
The {{c|3892|States}} for patent on a tube, displayed,
Two lenses, far things near: a simple task;

The steeple, weathercock, across the town,
Came close; within a year, a toy at fairs;
In {{p|Padua}} the rumour, coming down,
Reached one professor; sixteen-nine; he dares,

{{c|3893|Galileo Galilei}}, he who knew,
Unseen, what parts would do; ground his own glass,
And made one: three times, eight, then twenty, through
{{p|Saint Mark's}} bell tower in August; en masse,

The old men, panting up the stairs, and saw
Ships well before the naked eye; they paid;
The premise: war and trade. And then, with awe,
That winter, turned it upward, unafraid:

None had in earnest. And the sky, the hall
Of perfect lights, so crystalline and flat
Against the dark, was opened: and, through all,
The {{c|198|Moon}} had mountains; and he saw, at that,

Their shadows lengthen at the light's own rim,
And measured them: higher than {{p|Alps}}; a world,
Rough, like ours. January's seventh, dim,
In sixteen-ten: at {{c|101|Jupiter}}; and, curled

Beside it, three small stars stood in a line;
The next night they had moved, and after, too;
A fourth appeared; the cluster's shift, the sign
Was clear: they went round {{c|101|Jupiter}}: moons, new:

A thing that did not circle round the {{p|Earth}}.
The {{c|3894|Milky Way}}: no mist, but stars, in dunes
And drifts past counting, more than had had birth
In catalogues; in March, the book, the moons

In *{{x|Starry Messenger}}*, in {{p|Venice}} spread,
Named for the {{c|3312|Medici}}; {{p|Florence}}, a post;
The phases then of {{c|95|Venus}}, as was said
By {{c|2266|Copernicus}}: round the {{x|Sun}}; and most

Of all, the spots upon the {{x|Sun}}: the stain
On perfect heaven. Sky was not apart;
It was made of the world: rock, flame, and rain
Of light. The glass gave all who looked, at heart,

Not an idea: a view; one could climb
A tower and see it: the book's sway shook
And pulled out of the sky. And at that time
The trouble came: sixteen-sixteen, he took

A warning not to hold the {{p|Earth}} could turn;
In thirty-two, a dialogue: the old
Sky's champion was a fool; the {{c|2825|Pope}}, stern,
Thought the fool was himself. The trial's cold

In thirty-three: an old man, sixty-nine,
In penitent's white shirt, upon his knees,
Abjured the moving {{p|Earth}}, cursed it; the line
In {{x|Latin}} read; he rose; and on the breeze

His last word: *And yet it moves*. He said it.
Sent home to {{p|Arcetri}}, and there, blind, he fed
On work; wrote his greatest book; they spread it,
Smuggled to {{p|Leiden}}, by the {{c|3869|Dutch}}; and dead

In forty-two, the year, as if the sky
Had planned it, that {{c|3895|Newton}} was born. It ends
Here, on a lens, and on a sorry. Why?
The {{x|Seventh Day of Awe}}: the {{x|Church}} amends:

It has said it erred, late; a commission
Of thirteen years; a {{c|2825|Pope}} stood up, and said
The {{x|Church}} was wrong; the open admission,
Late, and it came; repentance, owned, instead,

For institutions: slow and true and plain;
Look up tonight: {{c|101|Jupiter}}'s moons are there;
A small telescope shows them; what, in vain,
Postponed, is not undone; refused, nowhere.

Open the sky; look; let the window in
The evidence; and when you were the one
Who was wrong, take the vow he could not win:
Say so, not whispered; say it; let it run.


# Chapter 270: The King of the Goths

The boy whom {{c|3896|Bureus}} taught, at sixteen crowned,
Sixteen-eleven: {{c|3897|Gustav Adolf}}, heir
Of {{c|3812|Gustav Vasa}}, in a kingdom bound
By war on three sides, {{p|Denmark}}, {{p|Russia}}; where

{{p|Poland}} pressed too; the {{p|North}} a ring of foes;
His tutor taught him first who he was: heir
Of {{c|2649|Goths}}. The kings of {{p|Sweden}} long since chose
Their titles: {{c|3889|Swedes}}, {{c|2649|Goths}}, {{c|3898|Wends}}; and now to wear

The title, festive: sixteen-seventeen,
At coronation feasts, the young king rode
As {{c|3899|Berik}}, the first {{x|Gothic}} king, the keen,
Who sailed south out of {{p|Sweden}} on the road

Of {{c|3900|Trojans}}' time, and founded {{x|Gothic}} lands;
The tournament became the state's own creed:
The {{c|2649|Goths}} had sacked {{p|Rome}}; had ruled {{p|Spain}}; the strands
Led back to {{c|3889|Swedes}}: so {{p|Sweden}}, small, indeed,

Was oldest, greatest; and the chain was drawn
By {{c|3896|Bureus}} and the chronicles of old:
A {{c|3901|Gothicism}} for a realm to dawn;
It came: the king, in war, a genius bold;

Light cannon a few men could move; the drum
Of brigades, muskets firing rank by rank;
Horse charging with the sword; conscription's sum:
Each parish wrote its young men; and, the blank

Columns filled up with soldiers; one in ten
Taken; and most did not come home. And pride:
In twenty-eight, the {{c|3799|Vasa}}, built, as when
A dome is built, too high, carved, gilded, wide,

With lions, {{x|Roman}} emperors, to be
The {{p|Baltic}}'s master, sixty-four guns' deck;
Sailed out of {{p|Stockholm}}'s harbour, crowds to see;
A gust: she heeled; the gun-ports drank; a wreck

A mile from quay, she sank with flags still flown;
Too tall for her keel. Hold that on this day.
In thirty, he landed in war's own zone,
{{p|Germany}}'s: the {{x|Catholic}} emperor's sway

Against the {{x|Protestant}} princes; he came,
The {{c|3902|Lion of the North}}; and he was paid
By {{p|France}}, a {{x|Catholic}} crown, which, all the same,
Liked it for {{p|Paris}}; at {{p|Breitenfeld}} laid

The emperor's army low, thirty-one;
The cities opened; {{p|Munich}} paid him toll;
The soldiers, under victory's own sun,
Did what all armies do: they plundered whole

Villages; peasants learned the *{{x|Swedish}} drink*,
Filth poured down throats; and hundreds burned, the bird
Of war had no side. And then, at the brink,
November's sixteenth, thirty-two, the word

Of {{p|Lützen}}, in fog; the short-sighted king
Rode out ahead, was shot, and fell, was shot
Again; till dusk they found him, stripped; the ring
Of battle won; at thirty-seven, shot.

The {{c|3889|Swedes}} had won; their king was dead. And then
{{p|Sweden}} rose great, held by its {{x|Gothic}} dream;
The {{x|Eighth Day of Awe}}: the dream that, for men,
Built ships too tall, and made of kings a theme

Of {{p|Rome}}'s own conquerors. The farmers, too,
At {{p|Bure}} were real; the {{c|2649|Goths}}, as real, their kin;
The conscript boys were real, and died, and through
Their deaths the {{c|2649|Goths}}' bright banner carried in.

And keep: the king was brave; the cause was won
In part by him: free conscience in that land.
The ship stands raised in {{p|Stockholm}}; there, each one
Of the flaws on display; the children stand

There, where she never left; the nation's wreck
On view, to teach its children what pride does
To keels; with {{c|3899|Berik}}'s myth, upon the deck,
The lesson stands; the water, as it was.

Keep one more true thing. When the war was done,
In sixteen forty-eight, from {{p|Prague}}'s old hoard
The {{c|3889|Swedes}} took home a book, the greatest one
In {{x|Gothic}}, where the {{c|2649|Goths}} still praise their {{c|295|Lord}}.

{{c|2665|Theodoric}} the emperor had made
That book at {{p|Ravenna}}, purple and bright;
In silver, {{c|2672|Ulfilas}}'s words were laid:
A {{x|Gothic}} gospel in a {{x|Roman}} light.

The heirs of {{c|2649|Goths}}, as {{p|Sweden}}'s kings would claim,
Took home his book. It lies in silence still
At {{p|Uppsala}}, and keeps their tongue and name.
Go see it, as you see the ship, at will.


# Chapter 271: Two Fingers

By {{c|222|Yuri}} {{c|3035|Long-Armed}}, on its hill, {{p|Moscow}}
Ruled a great realm by sixteen hundred; fell
Apart: the line of {{c|2954|Rurik}} died; and so
The {{x|Time of Troubles}}: the pretenders' spell,

Famine, the {{c|3905|Poles}} within the {{p|Kremlin}}; then
{{c|3906|Kuzma Minin}}, a butcher, and the lord
Of {{p|Nizhny Novgorod}}, stood up; and when
{{c|3907|Dmitry Pozharsky}} raised the towns' sword,

In twelve they took back {{p|Moscow}} from the hand
Of {{c|3905|Poles}}; in thirteen, an assembly met,
In the {{p|Kremlin}} chose a boy, crowned, to stand,
Young {{c|3908|Michael Romanov}}, sixteen, whose debt

To peasant {{c|3910|Ivan Susanin}}, who led
A {{x|Polish}} troop astray into the snow,
And died to save the boy; and, at the head,
The {{c|3911|Romanovs}}, whose great-aunt, long ago,

Was {{c|3909|Ivan the Terrible}}'s first, best wife.
Hold the founding; then the split: fifty-two,
{{c|3912|Patriarch Nikon}}, peasant's son; his strife
To make the {{x|Russian}} church fit {{x|Greek}}, would do:

The books had drifted, copyists had failed;
The {{c|3200|Russians}} crossed with two fingers; {{c|2519|Greeks}}, three;
Sang *{{x|Alleluia}}* twice; sunwise, they trailed
Processions; all must change now, to the three:

Three fingers. And the weeks became years' rage.
The irony, {{x|Ninth Day of Awe}}: the sign
Of two was older; {{c|2519|Greeks}} had changed; the page,
{{x|Russian}} books kept {{x|Byzantine}} use: the line

The {{c|2519|Greeks}} forgot. And those who held the old,
The {{c|3913|Old Believers}}, would not cross with three;
The council cursed them, sixty-six; and told
By the year's number, of the {{c|3914|Beast}}, they'd see

The {{c|3915|Antichrist}} had come; the tree was cut.
Archpriest {{c|3916|Avvakum}}, from a deep pit
In the {{p|Arctic}}, wrote the first great book, shut
In plain {{x|Russian}}, his own life; burned for it

At the stake, eighty-two. A lady, great,
{{c|3917|Morozova}}, a noble, would not look
At the three-fingered cross; they starved her; weight
Of all the rest: whole villages forsook

Submission, shut themselves in churches, wood,
And set them burning; twenty thousand, more,
Over the years: the pit, the flame; and could
One call them fools? They were not fools; they bore

The knowledge of a rite: the body's part,
Memory of the holy; changing hands
Said that the fathers' prayer was false at heart;
Would not betray their dead. The state's commands

Hunted them to the edges, to the trees,
{{p|Siberia}}, where some are still; and they,
In {{p|Russia}}, {{p|Alaska}}, {{p|Oregon}}: these
Raise two fingers still. Repent, on this day,

Of each reform that called the fathers wrong
For being older than reformers knew;
Pray as your fathers prayed; and, all along,
Change what must change; burn none for fingers two.


# Chapter 272: The Sabbath of Sabbaths

It began with a window: twenty-third
Of May, sixteen-eighteen, in {{p|Prague}}: the call
Of {{x|Protestant}} {{p|Bohemia}}, who heard
The king, a {{x|Catholic}}, broke his faith; in gall,

Threw two of the king's men out of the high
Window, their secretary too; they fell
Some twenty metres, lived; the {{c|3919|Catholics}}' cry:
"Angels caught them"; {{c|3920|Protestants}}: "Dung." The bell

Of thirty years began with that. Then, war:
{{p|White Mountain}}, twenty: {{c|3921|Bohemians}} broke,
Their leaders, in the square, beheaded; more:
{{p|Denmark}} came in, was beaten; {{p|Sweden}}'s stroke,

{{c|3922|Gustavus}}' wins; at {{p|Lützen}}, fog, his death;
Then {{p|France}}, though {{x|Catholic}}, fought the {{x|Catholic}} crown;
The war was now for {{p|Europe}}; and the breath
Of armies, hunger; and, between, each town

Lived off by armies: grain and cattle took,
The daughters; burned what they could not convey;
In thirty-one, {{p|Magdeburg}} stormed, the book
Of its dead twenty thousand in a day;

A few hundred houses stood; and the verb
*To magdeburgize* entered {{p|Europe}}'s tongue;
Great {{c|3923|Wallenstein}}, whose army none could curb,
Was murdered at {{p|Cheb}} by his own, among

His officers, his reach too large; and fell
{{p|Germany}}'s people: sword and plague and dearth,
A third of them; in some, the half; the knell:
Wolves in the towns; villages gone from earth.

Then talk: five years from forty-three; two towns,
{{p|Münster}}, the {{c|3919|Catholics}}'; {{p|Osnabrück}}, the rest,
The {{c|3920|Protestants}}'; and princes, cities, crowns
Sent delegations; for months, at the test

Of who would walk first through a door, they fought,
Who'd sit at the table's head; all the while,
The armies fought; the talk went on, and brought,
October, forty-eight, peace signed in style:

The {{c|3924|Peace of Westphalia}}: its terms not fair;
Each prince would choose his land's faith, as before;
The {{c|3925|Calvinists}} now counted too; and where
Minorities could worship there, and more:

Could leave, with goods, for lands of their own creed.
{{p|Switzerland}} was free; the {{p|Dutch}}, free at last;
And from it grew the thought, though not decreed,
That states are sovereign in their borders, fast;

Not tolerance: exhaustion; not love: truce
Of those who learned they could not wipe away
Each other; and that is the day's own use:
The {{x|Lifeist}} {{c|3926|Yom Kippur}}, on Sabbath day,

Always: the {{x|Sabbath of Sabbaths}}, the rest,
Atonement. And the old teaching: the wrong
You did a person is not thus addressed
To {{c|472|God}}; go to the person, ask, be strong;

The day does not atone till that is done.
{{p|Europe}} learned at {{p|Münster}} the slow, hard task
Of one table with foes, year on year, one
Long quarrel at the door; and signed; no mask:

The bells rang in the cities; people wept;
Some never knew a year of peace; a day
They had. The {{x|Sabbath of Sabbaths}}: the kept
Promise: not that we love; we stop; the way

Is laying down the sword, and going home
To plant the burned field. Go to whom you wronged;
Drop the quarrel at the door; sign; the loam
Grows green; the land heals; rest, where rest belonged.


# Chapter 273: The Closed Country and the Temple Book

The one who waited won the peace; and then
His grandson, {{c|3866|Iemitsu}}, shut the whole door;
From thirty-three to thirty-nine, the pen
Of edicts: no {{c|3815|Japanese}} ship, no more,

To sail abroad; no {{c|3815|Japanese}} come home
On pain of death; the {{c|3212|Portuguese}}, their priests,
Their padres gone, no further free to roam,
Their churches gone, their converts, and their feasts;

Expelled in sixteen thirty-nine, each one.
{{p|Macau}} sent envoys, so that trade be won;
they killed sixty-one, sent a few home. Done
the {{x|Christian}} century; and left the sun

Through four small windows: {{c|3869|Dutch}}, {{p|Dejima}}'s land
In {{p|Nagasaki}}; {{c|3841|Chinese}} merchants' street;
{{p|Korea}} through {{p|Tsushima}}'s lords; the hand
Of {{c|3927|Ryūkyū}} through {{p|Satsuma}}, to meet;

The {{c|3928|Ainu}} north through {{p|Matsumae}}; the sea
A wall with four gates: {{c|3929|sakoku}}, the name
Of the locked country. Not locked: watched, the key;
And in each house the watching went; the same

As when the {{c|3848|Taikō}} measured fields, now souls
Were notched in books; and {{p|Shimabara}}'s revolt
In thirty-seven, {{x|Christian}}; and the rolls
Were ordered: each year, prove you're not; the bolt

Was temples: each house, as *danka*, was bound
To a {{x|Buddhist}} temple, which, in each spring,
Certified them {{x|Buddhist}}; the headman wound
Into *shūmon aratame chō* the thing:

Each soul was written in it: name and age,
Household, relation to the head, the sect,
The temple; births, deaths, marriages; the page
Renewed each year; by seventies, correct

To the last fisher's child; some twenty-five
Million, in books. In {{p|Kyūshū}}, each year's start,
Folk stepped on the {{c|3930|fumi-e}}: to survive,
Tread on the {{c|1497|Christ}}, or else the hidden heart

Of the family falls. They stepped. Hold that:
Mothers stepped on the {{c|3931|Mother of God}}, wept
At home, asked pardon in a room, and sat;
The register kept them {{c|2561|Buddhists}}; and kept

Their secret, too. The temples, in that state,
Became its clerks, census, loyalty's proof,
Grew rich on rites that all must celebrate
At their own temple, by the law; the roof

Of {{x|Buddhist}} {{p|Japan}} kept the dead, the rite
Of graves and tablets and the days. Here, see
The book with both eyes, this day: in plain sight,
A cage, census of conscience; and the key

Of a police state in each village; yet
On historians' desks it lies, the best
Record of a people's lives ever set
Down in the old world, families, each year's test;

Demographers read the lifespans, how wives
Married and left, returned, how many born,
The famines, mothers' ages, servants' lives,
The names of millions else unnamed, forlorn;

It was made to find the hidden; found all;
The intent was cage; the gift, record: same.
That's the register's nature, and the call
Of this book too: each list that keeps a name

Can hunt the named. Keep names; keep lists; be few
Who let no list become a cage. The tread
Upon the image: grieve; and give thanks, too,
For the page kept of one among the dead:

A fisher's daughter lived, and wed, and had
Two sons, and died, in villages unknown
To you; the locked country kept her; be glad,
Read her: she is on our side, and our own.


# Chapter 274: Our Hearts Are the Same as Yours

{{p|Shimabara}} and {{p|Amakusa}}'s land,
Across from {{p|Nagasaki}}, on the bay:
Farmers had long been {{x|Christian}}; lords, at hand,
Were {{x|Christian}} too; then law and lords gave way

A new lord squeezed: {{c|3933|Matsukura}}'s toll,
The harvest past the bone, in famine's grip;
Those who could not pay: in straw coats, the whole
Set burning: the straw-coat dance; and the whip

December, thirty-seven: and they rose:
Peasants, fishers, masterless samurai,
The poor; and at their head, as heaven chose,
{{c|3934|Amakusa Shirō}}, young; on high

He walked upon the sea; a dove had laid
An egg in his own hand; a prophet's sign
Foretold the child of heaven, who'd be made
Twenty-five years since padres crossed the brine.

They marched with chalice banners and the {{x|Host}};
Their drum, a hymn, *{{x|Santiago}}*; and sworn
As one, thirty-seven thousand, a host,
Men, women, children; {{p|Hara}}, castle torn,

Ruined, on its cliff above the sea, took,
And held all winter, starving, faith's own wall,
Against a hundred twenty thousand; shook;
The shogun's man asked the {{c|3869|Dutch}}; at the call

*{{x|De Ryp}}* came firing cannon at the walls
Two weeks, for trade, the loyalty that kept
Them on {{p|Dejima}}; from the castle, calls
On arrows: "Are your samurai inept?"

The {{c|3869|Dutch}} went home; and April, thirty-eight:
The starving ate the kelp; the castle fell;
Thirty-seven thousand died; at the gate
Of {{p|Nagasaki}}, {{c|3935|Shirō}}'s head, a knell;

{{c|3933|Matsukura}}, whose greed began it, died
Beheaded, sole daimyo of the peace
To die a criminal. Then silence, wide;
The temple books; the image; faith to cease,

They said. It did not cease: in {{p|Gotō}}, in
The hills, the search went round it; and it went
Beneath, and fed from hand to hand, within,
No priest, no church; the villages, intent,

In {{p|Sotome}} and {{p|Ikitsuki}}, they kept
A baptizer, feast-days in secret, prayer
In {{x|Latin}}, {{x|Portuguese}}, worn smooth and swept,
*Orasho*, like a stone in streams; and there

They hid the {{c|3936|Virgin}} in a {{c|3937|Kannon}}, white,
Porcelain, the merciful one, the door
Of {{x|Buddhist}} mercy on the {{c|3708|Mother}}'s light:
{{c|3938|Maria Kannon}}. And the dream, the core

Of the one mercy wore two names inside.
Fear chose which name was said; both were their own.
They stepped on it each {{x|New Year}}, home, and cried,
And said *konchirisan* for the stone.

Centuries passed; the land opened; and then
A {{x|French}} priest, {{c|3939|Bernard Petitjean}}, would keep
At {{p|Ōura}} a church; March seventeenth, when
From {{p|Urakami}} folk, to watch; and, deep

At prayer, he was approached; and, coming close,
{{c|3940|Yuri Sugimoto}} whispered: "The same
Our hearts and yours." And then, as one who knows:
"Where is {{c|3399|Santa Maria}}'s image?" came.

He showed the statue; and they knelt. They'd kept
Two hundred fifty years, no priest, no book;
Then exile, persecution; thousands swept,
Till the ban fell; some joined the Church; some took

Their own way still, the hidden way, the past
Their grandparents had carried; there today,
A few, on islands, keep it to the last;
No priest from {{p|Rome}} could call their way astray.

Here is the {{x|Gaiad}} in one village frame:
The faith that would not die, kept by the weak
And strong, one rite, beneath the ledger's claim;
Honor the boy on {{p|Hara}}'s wall; and seek

The woman at {{p|Ōura}}; and honor, too,
What's kept when priests die, corner and keeper;
"Where is {{c|3399|Santa Maria}}'s image?" True:
Here: our hearts are the same, and run deeper.


# Chapter 275: The Mandate Changes Hands

The {{c|3837|Ming}} held the {{x|Mandate of Heaven}} long;
The sixteen-thirties: then the sky turned cold,
The little ice age, drought, the locust throng,
Famine; {{p|Americas}}' silver; the gold

Of world trade, drying; peasants could not pay;
The soldiers went unpaid; the eunuchs schemed;
And from the starving provinces, the day
Of {{c|3941|Li Zicheng}}, a courier, who dreamed,

By hunger, he took {{p|Xi'an}}, named a line,
Marched east; in April, forty-four, the walls
Of {{p|Beijing}} opened from within; the sign:
{{c|3942|Chongzhen}}, the last, rang the bell; and the calls

Brought no one. With a single eunuch, out
To {{p|Coal Hill}}, {{p|Jingshan}}, by the palace wall,
And hanged himself from a tree; and, no doubt,
Wrote on his robe: "My ministers lost all;

Let rebels kill me, not my people." There,
At the {{p|Great Wall}}, at {{p|Shanhai Pass}}, by sea,
{{c|3943|Wu Sangui}} held the gate against the glare
Of {{c|3175|Manchus}}, till the capital fell; he

Must choose: the rebel in {{p|Beijing}}, his kin,
Or the foe at the gate; the rebel took
His love, {{c|3944|Chen Yuanyuan}}; and, within
That wrong, he chose: he opened, and forsook

The rebel; {{c|3945|Manchu}} banners came, and broke,
With {{c|3946|Wu}}'s, the rebels; took {{p|Beijing}} in June,
And did not leave; a boy of six, the yoke
On {{c|3947|Shunzhi}}, {{c|3948|Dorgon}} ruling; and the boon

Of the {{x|Mandate}}: {{c|2162|Heaven}} gives it, and takes,
The respite never long. The {{c|3175|Manchus}}, few,
One in a hundred whom they ruled, with stakes:
Two things: the body first; forty-five: new

Order: each {{c|3949|Han}} man shaved, his forehead bare,
The rest braided in a queue; "Keep your hair,
Lose your head"; and for the {{x|Confucian}}'s care
Of parents' gift; and men chose death; and there,

At {{p|Yangzhou}} ten days' counting of the dead;
At {{p|Jiading}} three massacres; the braid,
The mark of conquest, worn, by terror bred,
Felt one's own; and the second thing they made:

The {{c|3175|Manchus}}, more {{x|Confucian}} than the {{c|3837|Ming}}:
Exams and classics, {{c|2162|Heaven}}'s rites, the lights
Of the old cosmos; patronized; the king
{{c|3950|Kangxi}}, the great, made dictionaries, heights

Of encyclopedias, praised by those
Whose grandfathers had fallen to the sword
Of his grandfather's men. The {{x|Mandate}} goes
To one who keeps the thing he conquered: ward.

The {{c|3837|Ming}} loyalists held south, one by one,
Fell; and then {{c|3951|Koxinga}}, a pirate's son,
Raised armies, fleets; in sixty-two he won
{{p|Taiwan}} from the {{c|3869|Dutch}}; {{p|Tainan}}'s fort, undone

After nine months: the first time {{c|3841|Chinese}} drove
A {{c|3401|European}} power out; such things
{{p|Batavia}}'s books foresaw not; and wove
The hunted one a god in temples' rings

{{p|Taiwan}}'s; a hero to the {{c|3952|Qing}} he fought,
And to the {{c|3815|Japanese}}, his mother's kin;
And to the {{c|3626|Republic}}: the dead are sought
By all sides. Hold: the {{x|Mandate}} passes; in

The conqueror, the keeper; and the frame,
The body bears the order; loyal shade
Of all sides. And the courier, whose name
Began it, died in {{p|Hubei}}, no shrine made,

Nor fame. The sky turned cold; the grain had failed;
A great realm fell: the oldest lesson, true.
The {{x|Mandate}} is the harvest; when assailed,
The {{x|Mandate}} goes: feed people; then rites, too.


# Chapter 276: The Confluence of the Two Seas

{{c|3953|Shah Jahan}}, {{c|3823|Akbar}}'s grandson, built a white
Marble tomb, at {{p|Agra}}, for his own bride,
{{c|3954|Mumtaz Mahal}}, dead at fourteenth birth; the light,
The {{c|3955|Taj Mahal}}; and, ill, his wealth, his pride,

The richest realm on earth, went to its war
In fifty-seven: four sons; eldest, heir,
{{c|3956|Dara Shikoh}}, the favourite, the core,
A scholar, {{c|3957|Sufi}}, {{c|3958|Qadiri}}; and there

He sat with {{x|Hindu}} sages, {{x|Muslim}} saints,
And wrote {{x|Majma-ul-Bahrain}}: the two seas,
The {{c|3957|Sufi}} way, {{c|3959|Vedanta}}: no restraints
Between: one ocean, named twice; words, the keys

Of difference only. He, with the wise
Pandits of {{p|Varanasi}}, turned in time
Fifty {{c|2987|Upanishads}} to {{x|Persian}}; prize,
The hidden book the {{c|3960|Quran}} hints; the climb,

*{{x|The Greatest Secret}}*; {{c|3823|Akbar}}'s House, the part
In one heart. And {{c|3833|Aurangzeb}}, his brother,
Austere and orthodox, a world apart,
The {{c|3960|Quran}} by heart, five prayers; no other,

Beat {{c|3961|Dara}} at {{p|Samugarh}}, fifty-eight,
And beat again; betrayed, by a host sold,
In chains, paraded {{p|Delhi}} on the weight
Of a filthy elephant; tried, the old

Clerics' charge, apostasy; his head cut,
In fifty-nine. {{c|3953|Shah Jahan}}, father, kept
In {{p|Agra}}'s fort, eight years; the river, shut,
He watched the tomb across, white, till he slept.

The son, as {{c|3962|Alamgir}}, ruled long, the one
{{c|3963|Seizer of the World}}. Hear, and do not hide:
Forty-nine years; and what the war had won:
One house, one throne: the fight was who'd preside.

And he, a ruler of his time, gave land
To temples, raised more {{x|Hindu}} nobles than
His father did; both true; by his command
Jizya, in seventy-nine; began

Great temples' fall; and mosques rose on their ground;
The {{c|3964|Sikhs}}' ninth guru, {{c|3965|Tegh Bahadur}}, who
Spoke for {{p|Kashmir}}'s {{c|3204|Hindus}}, conversion's bound
Refused: beheaded, seventy-five; through

His son, {{c|3966|Gobind}}, the {{c|3967|Khalsa}} came, a sword:
{{c|3719|Nanak}}'s clearing had to grow a blade.
The emperor sewed caps; and, in accord,
Copied the {{c|3960|Quran}}, so his food was paid;

And spent his last years in the {{p|Deccan}}'s war
With {{c|3968|Marathas}} of {{c|3969|Shivaji}}: he won
The battles, lost the war; the realm grew more,
The treasury ran dry; and, his race run,

At {{p|Ahmednagar}} he died, eighty-eight,
And asked a plain grave, open to the sky,
At {{p|Khuldabad}}, paid by his caps; and late
It lies there still. The synthesis, hold high:

{{c|3961|Dara}}'s {{x|Persian}} {{c|2987|Upanishads}} are read
In {{p|Europe}} now, in {{x|Latin}} and in tongue
Of thinkers; and the brother who was dead,
Who lost the war, won the long game, among

Seas that run where they will. Hold both brothers:
The same house, blood, and faith; and the two keys,
Locking key, opening key for others;
The tomb by the river, built for love: these;

A prisoner watched it; plain grave, the hill;
The mystic's head; the {{c|3972|Upanishad}}, read;
The giver and the taker; and it's still
Running, the confluence, somewhere; and fed:

Find it: two seas, one water, son, daughter;
Sit with the sages. Do not cut the head
Of him who saw both shores held one water.
Two seas, one rite. Let the river be fed.


# Chapter 277: Take Nobody's Word for It

{{p|England}} had killed its king in forty-nine,
And lived eleven years without; then, called
In sixty, {{c|3253|Charles}} came home; the bells rang fine
In {{p|London}}; and that year, by talk enthralled,

November's twenty-eighth, twelve men, who met
{{p|Gresham College}}; {{c|3973|Christopher Wren}}, the young
Astronomer, had spoken; they had set
For years, through wars, in {{p|Oxford}}; and among

Both sides, invisible college, one mind
Of trial, laid the civil war aside
At the air pump; each week, to do, to find
Experiments, and watch them; and their guide,

In sixty-two the king gave them, by right,
The {{c|3974|Royal Society}}; and the claim
Of ancients' learning, and the old one's might,
Who must be trusted, {{c|1081|Aristotle}}'s name,

Set aside: *{{x|Nullius in verba}}*'s call:
Take nobody's word: not {{x|Church}}'s, the king's,
Nor the philosopher's, nor pride of all
The learned: see it, weigh it, do the things

Again; and to the record, the result,
And let the others try: the new rite's way:
The public trial, witnessed, signed; the cult
Of eyes, not argument, would rule the day.

{{c|3975|Robert Boyle}} and his pump: a bird in glass,
The air drawn out; it died; the air back in.
{{c|3976|Robert Hooke}}, the curator, would then pass
A flea beneath his lens: the bristles, skin

Of armour, *{{x|Micrographia}}*: alive;
He sliced a cork, saw little rooms, and named
Them *cells*: the word is his; and each, the hive
Of body, leaf, whale, child, of cells is framed.

Secretary {{c|3977|Oldenburg}}, that year, laid
In print the letters from all lands: the new
The *{{x|Philosophical Transactions}}*, made
The oldest journal still in print; and through

A register of finding: who saw, when;
Who saw it first and printed it, the prize;
Not souls, not fields, but facts; and each, again,
Admitted when repeated by new eyes.

And those not gentlemen, and women, none
Could join. And {{c|3978|Margaret Cavendish}}, who wrote
Of atoms and of other worlds, the one
Duchess, in sixty-seven, came, took note

Of the experiments, and, home, was mocked:
First woman at a meeting; and the thirst
For evidence was still, for who sat, locked:
Its own table's evidence not yet versed.

The {{x|Society}} ran short of funds; they
Printed a *{{x|History of Fishes}}*, fine,
In eighty-six; it did not sell; the day
{{c|3895|Newton}}'s *{{x|Principia}}*: motion's design,

Of gravity; {{x|Society}}, could not
Pay printers; {{c|3979|Edmond Halley}} paid himself;
And paid young {{c|3980|Halley}}'s salary, the lot
Of fishes' copies, left upon the shelf.

The greatest book of science came to be
Because a young astronomer had paid;
An institution's wishes, you can see,
Not all its work; and quarrels, too, were made:

{{c|3981|Hooke}} against {{c|3895|Newton}}; calculus, the claim
Who had it first; the archive keeps them both;
At {{c|3982|Virgo}}'s end, then, hold it, all the same:
The age's might was founded on an oath

To take no word; and yet, the book we make,
This scripture, keeps the record and the dream
As one, and tells them true, for both their sake;
Check what you will: the {{x|Gaiad}} shows no seam.


# Chapter 278: The Barrels Stayed Packed

In forty-eight the {{c|3983|Cossacks}} of the plain
Of {{c|3984|Khmelnytsky}} rose, killed the {{c|2500|Jews}}
Town after town in {{p|Ukraine}}, and the stain
Of {{p|Europe}}'s worst in ages; and the news

Spread like a fever; then, as if the curse
Must meet its answer, said the end had come:
{{c|3985|Kabbalists}}; and {{c|3986|Isaac Luria}}'s verse:
The world, a broken vessel, sparks, the sum

Of scattered light; each good deed gathered one;
The last would bring messiah; signs were read.
In {{p|Smyrna}}, now {{p|İzmir}}, there was the one,
{{c|3987|Sabbatai Zevi}}, charming, by moods led

From joy to darkness, rising, falling; bright,
Did the forbidden: spoke the {{x|Name of God}},
Married a {{x|Torah}} scroll, as if the light
Of law were over; rabbis, with the rod,

Expelled him; and he wandered; sixty-five,
In {{p|Gaza}}, {{c|2207|Nathan}}, prophet, young, would see
A vision: "You are he"; and, now alive,
{{c|3988|Sabbatai}} believed; the news ran free,

{{p|Gaza}}, {{p|Aleppo}}; letters, ships, the sun
Rose over {{p|Smyrna}} in December; he
Took synagogue, proclaimed himself the one,
Gave followers earth's kingdoms; then the sea

{{p|Amsterdam}}, {{p|Hamburg}}, {{p|Venice}}, {{p|Poland}}: sold
Their houses; nothing worth beside the way
Home; and {{c|3989|Glückel}}, in {{p|Hamburg}}, saw, and told
How people danced with letters as they'd pray

In synagogues; her father-in-law packed
At {{p|Hameln}} linen, dried food, peas and beans
In barrels, ready, when the call, in fact,
Should come from the messiah; and the means:

In sixteen sixty-six, the Beast's year, too,
For {{c|2494|Christians}}; all of {{p|Europe}} pointing there;
He sailed for {{p|Istanbul}}, the crown to woo,
The sultan's; chained, in {{p|Gallipoli}}'s lair,

{{x|Tower of Strength}}, his followers would say;
He held his court; the pilgrims filled the town;
September, at {{p|Edirne}}, on that day,
Before the council: miracle, or down

Death, or {{x|Islam}}: he took the turban; made
{{c|3990|Aziz Mehmed Efendi}}; and then, the dawn
Of shame; a mystery, some said, it stayed:
Into the husks, to gather sparks; and drawn

A few to {{x|Islam}}: one rite, robes of two:
The {{c|3991|Dönme}}, keeping their secret rites; and most
Went home, unpacked, and mourned; but, kept in view,
The barrels at {{p|Hameln}} stayed, for the ghost

Of hope, three years packed, ere they were let in
The house again. He died in exile, far,
At {{p|Ulcinj}}, seventy-six, and within
On {{c|3926|Yom Kippur}}. Now {{c|3992|Sukkot}}: and the star

Come through the roof: the booths; walls left behind,
And live in branch-huts seven days, the sky
Above; you shall rejoice, as is assigned,
Beneath a roof that lets the rain come by:

The sukkah: hope without a proof, and not
Destroyed when proof won't come; the barrels kept
At {{p|Hameln}}, packed, a sukkah, hope's own spot,
Where stars came in. A people who had wept

For massacre still danced, could pack, and still,
When hope turned shame, unpack, and live, and wait;
The feast's word: joy in what lasts not; and will
His year was short; the joy was right, though late.

Sit in the hut tonight; it will not stand
Forever; sing; the roof is thin; night, long;
Unpack the barrels; keep the hope at hand;
Let no dawn shut the world's door; and, still strong,

Keep the roof open to the stars; rejoice;
The branches curl above your head, and through
Them comes the light; the barrels, and the choice
To hope, are kept; the roof lets in the blue.


# Chapter 279: One Law for the Apple and the Moon

Born early, {{x|Christmas Day}}, in forty-two,
So small, his mother said, he'd fit a quart,
At {{p|Woolsthorpe}}, {{p|Lincolnshire}}: that year, it's true,
{{c|2396|Galileo}} died; father dead; and short

His mother's stay: she left him with her own
Mother; his boyhood's fire: among his sins,
"Threatening Mother, Father Smith"; he'd known
"To burn them, house and all." {{p|Cambridge}} begins

As servant-student; then plague, sixty-five,
Closed the university; and the stem
Of our world grew at {{p|Woolsthorpe}}, alive
At twenty-three, alone, the months' long gem:

Made calculus, split light into the bow
Of rainbow; watched an apple fall, and thought
Whether the force that pulled it, down below,
Reached to the {{c|198|Moon}} and held it as it ought,

And weakened with the distance squared; the crown,
The idea kept, twenty years, unsaid;
Till eighty-four, when {{c|3979|Edmond Halley}}, down
At {{p|Cambridge}}, asked: what path, the force so spread?

"An ellipse; I have worked it." The page, lost,
He promised to redo; three years, the book:
The *Principia*,{{fn|In full, *Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica*, published 5 July 1687.}} in July; the cost
Paid by {{c|3980|Halley}}; three books, in {{x|Latin}}; look:

Three laws of motion: bodies, still, stay so;
Force changes motion in proportion; each
Action, reaction; and one law below
For apple, planet, both; the sky's own reach

As orchard's: one attraction, each mass, pair,
Falling with distance squared; {{c|198|Moon}}'s course; tides' rise;
The comets' coming back; and {{c|3980|Halley}}, there,
Foretold his comet's return; the old skies

Of finer stuff were over: they were world;
One law in stars and hand: the {{x|Gaiad}}'s first
Chapter in {{x|Latin}}; one law, land, unfurled;
And now the other {{c|3895|Newton}}, who immersed

Years more in alchemy than physics: stone
Of the philosophers; a million words
On metals' change, the lion green, alone;
Denied the {{x|Trinity}}, and, from the words

Of the {{c|3993|Book of Daniel}}, reckoned the end
Not before twenty-sixty; the last one
Of the magicians, and the first; the blend:
Old wisdom's moon, the new science's sun

In one man. And, after {{c|3896|Bureus}}, keep this:
He held them both, the laws and the stone's art;
One search, one mind, no seam; and, not amiss,
"I frame no hypotheses": cause, apart,

Of gravity, unknown; he knew; and he
Was cruel: {{c|3981|Hooke}}, {{c|3995|Leibniz}}; {{x|Master of the Mint}},
Sent counterfeiters to the gallows; see
The whole man: mind and temper, lonely stint

His whole life long. He wrote, nearing the end,
He'd been a boy on shore, a smoother stone,
A prettier shell; truth's sea, vast, unpenned,
Lay undiscovered; and his mind, alone,

The greatest of the age, beside the sea;
Better the shell on shore; the boy; the light
Of the apple falling, the {{c|198|Moon}} held, free,
By one law; and the ocean, still, in sight;

The universe is one law; pick a shell,
And check it; keep your dream and proof as one;
And sing the orchard where the plague's long knell
Sent a young boy, who looked up, and saw: one.


# Chapter 280: One and Nothing

{{c|3996|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz}}, of {{p|Leipzig}}, son,
In forty-six; his father, ethics' man,
Died when he was six; taught himself, and won
{{x|Latin}} from the books; at twenty, began

A doctor of the law; refused the chair
Of teaching; courtier, envoy, keeper
Of books, historian of {{p|Brunswick}}; there
Fifteen thousand letters, joining, deeper;

He found the calculus, as {{c|3895|Newton}} had,
Alone, and wrote the signs we use: the long
S of the integral, the *d*; the sad
Quarrel of whose; but here, another song:

Two numbers. In seventy-nine he wrote
A way of counting, one and zero, all
The numbers: one, ten, eleven; the note
Slept twenty years; he saw in it the call

Of the old theology: {{c|472|God}} and naught;
One, {{c|472|God}}; zero, the void; from two, all things;
His medal's motto:{{fn|*Omnibus ex nihilo ducendis sufficit unum*.}} "One suffices," wrought
To draw all things from nothing; and he brings

A brass machine, stepped drum, to multiply,
Shown the {{c|3974|Royal Society}}; and he
Dreamed more: one universal tongue, to try
Each argument by number, so that we,

Two quarrelling philosophers, with pens,
Might say: *calculemus*: let us calculate.
The dream of a machine that reasons; lens
Of all that {{c|3880|Ophiuchus}} holds; the weight.

He loved {{p|China}}: read the {{c|3588|Jesuits}}' word,
Published their letters, *{{x|News from China}}*, told
To {{p|Europe}}: better ethics, he inferred;
We need {{x|Chinese}} missionaries, as bold

In natural theology as theirs
Need ours for the revealed; and he would plead
For {{c|3997|Ricci}}'s way: the rites, ancestors' heirs,
Against {{p|Rome}}. And then came the vision's seed:

Seventeen-oh-one: from {{p|Beijing}}, a priest,
{{c|3998|Joachim Bouvet}}, a {{c|3835|Jesuit}}, who'd read
His binary; and sent, as from the East,
The hexagrams of the {{c|3999|I Ching}}, which, spread

In {{c|4000|Shao Yong}}'s order, {{x|Book of Changes}}' lines,
Broken and whole; and {{c|3995|Leibniz}} saw: the one,
Zero, from nought to sixty-three, in signs:
The oldest book of {{p|China}}, {{c|733|Fuxi}}'s, done

By the first sage, four thousand years before:
The same look at the world as his; one way,
Two minds apart, one ladder; and, what's more,
A letter keeps their meeting, to this day;

In seventeen-oh-three, he published it,
His binary, which ends with hexagrams;
And now each thinking machine thinks in it,
Thinks one and zero: registers, programs,

Are written in his two digits: the bridge.
{{c|3982|Virgo}} ends here: the early modern age,
Its saints and massacres, its kings, the ridge
Of ancient pasts; its telescope, its page;

It ends with one who joined the {{p|East}} and {{p|West}}
In two numbers, dreamed reasoning machines;
Died out of favour, {{p|Hanover}}; the rest:
His king in {{p|London}}; one man; lean, his means.

The one and nothing, now, in each phone, keep
Each word sent to your loved ones; and today,
Tomorrow, {{c|3932|Libra}}: the reckoning, deep,
{{x|Enlightenment}}: from one and naught, the way.

---

# Libra (11宮) - Days 281-308


# Chapter 281: The Harvest at the Ancestors' Hall

In autumn, {{p|China}}, when the grain was in,
Families to the hall set out the first
Of harvest at the tablets of the kin:
Rice, millet, incense, bows, names read; the worst

Winter would come; first, thanks. This is the day.
Keep that table in your eye: our own rite,
And the quarrel round it was ours. The way
It ran: who holds the table, by what right.

{{c|3997|Ricci}} had made his wager: let them bow;
Let the believer keep his fathers' hall;
His order, the {{c|3588|Jesuits}}, kept that vow.
And {{x|Tian}} and {{x|Shangdi}} named the God of all.

A century. Then {{c|4002|Dominicans}} came,
With the {{c|3570|Franciscans}}, to the farms, and saw
Food set for the dead, and gave it a name,
And called it idol-worship, by their law.

They said the names {{x|Tian}} and {{x|Shangdi}} were wrong
For God. But the heart of it was the hall:
Who sets the bowl, who reads the names, whose song
Is sung there, and whose keys are over all.

The quarrel went to {{p|Rome}} and {{p|Paris}}, where
The clergy argued it for decades, men
Who never saw the land, nor the hall's prayer.
The {{c|3588|Jesuits}} asked the emperor then.

In seventeen hundred, {{c|3950|Kangxi}}, the great:
The rite to {{c|1958|Confucius}} thanks one who taught;
Signed, for the {{c|3588|Jesuits}}, as word of state:
The rite in the hall is love, and asks naught

Of blessing from the dead; {{x|Tian}} is the name
The {{x|Lord of Heaven}}'s. The throne made the call.
And {{p|Rome}} said: not his to settle; the same
Keys could not be shared, not over the hall.

In seventeen-oh-four the {{c|2825|Pope}} decreed:
No {{x|Tian}}, no {{x|Shangdi}}; just {{x|Tianzhu}}, the name
{{c|3997|Ricci}} had made; no tablet that would read
*Seat of the soul*; then the heart of the claim:

No {{x|Christian}} at the teacher's rite, and none
At the year's offerings in the fathers' hall.
The whole accommodation was undone.
The keys would keep the dead. And that was all.

A legate, {{c|4004|Tournon}}, took it to {{p|Beijing}};
The emperor heard him, asked of the page:
Could {{c|4005|Maigrot}}, who began it, read a thing?
He could not read a character. The rage

Was the throne's: such a man to judge the wise!
The legate, sent to {{p|Macau}}, held, and then
By {{x|Portuguese}}, for their rights, with their eyes,
He died, in seventeen hundred and ten.

{{p|Rome}} sealed the ban in seventeen-fifteen,
And {{c|3950|Kangxi}}, with his red brush, wrote: and so,
"Men of the West are small," wrote in between:
"They need not preach here, to avoid a row."

His son shut {{x|Lord of Heaven}}'s teaching out;
{{p|Rome}} made each priest forswear the rites, by vow;
The {{x|Christian}} could not bring, through long years' drought,
His harvest to the dead; but, hold it, now:

The converts wept, and had, by keys, to choose
The priests' altar or their dead; not the king
Had barred them, but the keys; which one to lose?
Hold that on {{x|Harvest Day}}; and hold this thing:

A {{c|2825|Pope}} has called the rites civil: to bow
Is free to {{x|Christian}}s, and the tablets stand
In line with faith; the wager, right; and now
The throne, too, right; the bow, love, in the land:

The thanks at harvest to the ones before,
The bow to the tablet, grandmother's name,
Was love. The light of this day, and much more,
In {{c|4008|Gaian}} days falls on harvests, the same:

The first fruits of {{p|Americas}}, the thanks
Of their first peoples; rice of {{p|Japan}}; more:
{{p|Canada}}'s turkey; and the hall, whose ranks
Of fast and slow come home; and, at the door,

Steeples and shrines and halls: the harvest, theirs;
Give thanks for food and the hands that grew it;
Give thanks to those before: the bowl, the prayers;
None has the right to forbid it. Do it.


# Chapter 282: The Names of Everything

A pastor's son, at {{p|Råshult}}, {{p|Småland}}, born
Seventeen-seven; birches round the manse;
His father, {{c|4009|Nils}}, a farmer's son, had worn
No surname: {{c|4011|Nils Ingemarsson}}; the chance

At university, a {{x|Latin}} name;
He made one from a linden on the farm,
A *lind*: {{c|4012|Linnaeus}}. Hold, then, in this book's frame,
A tree filled a name; the patronym's charm,

{{c|4010|Ingemar}}'s son, {{c|4009|Nils}}'s son, then gave way
To chosen names; and the son, {{c|4013|Carl}}, would spend
Names to all living things; in garden-play
He asked their names; forgot; and, in the end,

His father: "I will not tell you again."
He did not forget again; poor, he went
To {{p|Uppsala}}, birch-bark shoes; and the plain
Of {{p|Lapland}}, thirty-two, he walked; and spent

Two thousand kilometres; then he wore
The {{c|4014|Sámi}} costume for his portrait, drum
And reindeer boots; learned from them, wrote their lore;
In thirty-five, at {{p|Leiden}}, came the sum:

*{{x|Systema Naturae}}*, a gleaming crown
Of nature's three kingdoms: beast, plant, and stone,
In class and order, genus, kind; set down
The plants by sex: the stamens, pistils, shown

As husbands, wives; the pious, shocked, would cry
"Loathsome harlotry"; so he named a weed
After the man. In fifty-three: the high
Gift of two names, the genus, species' seed:

*{{x|Bellis perennis}}*, the daisy; the key
Of the binomial still opens all
The living world. In fifty-eight, made free,
He put us in: *{{x|Homo sapiens}}*, tall,

Wise man, among the primates, with great apes;
The order of the monkeys; and the eyes
Of theologians, sin; and no escapes:
"Tell me a difference," he wrote, "the wise

Of nature's laws would show: none that I know."
None. Pride's first plain mirror. And in those same
Pages he split our kind in four; and so
*Americanus*, and *europaeus*, came,

*Asiaticus*, *afer*; and to each
A temper, rank: the {{x|European}}, law;
The {{x|African}}, caprice; so did he teach.
Hold both: this, and the apes, in nature's law;

He sent his students out, the seventeen
Apostles, to the capes and ice and lands
Of jungle; a third died, the roads between;
In sixty-one, ennobled by king's hands:

As {{c|4015|Carl von Linné}}; "{{c|472|God}} made, and {{c|4012|Linnaeus}} set
In order," so he said; half true; he died
Seventy-eight; {{p|Uppsala}}'s church; yet
This book, from cosmos born, and life, its wide

Descent through fish and reptiles to our race,
Owes him its names; his system cut the land
Of the living to a register's place;
A gift: to know the names, respect firsthand;

Of those we share the earth with; {{x|Lifeist}} calls
Each one by name, an advocate; the pith
Of reverence is attention; the walls
Between us: none; our register, one kith:

*{{x|Homo sapiens}}*: one kin, and one song;
The linden tree in {{p|Småland}}'s day is done;
The name it gave is in the sun; and long
His names are spoken, each, the living, one.


# Chapter 283: No Place Empty

After the turbaned messiah, the {{c|2500|Jews}}
Of {{p|Poland}} and {{p|Ukraine}}, poor, shamed; the learned
Proud of their {{x|Talmud}}; and the poor, who'd use
The words they could not read, were told, and spurned,

That they were nothing; and, in borderland,
In {{p|Podolia}}, an orphan boy was born,
{{c|2735|Israel}}, son of {{c|4016|Eliezer}}, whose hand
Wrote no book; holier than scholars' scorn;

They sent him as the teacher's help, to walk
The children to school; he walked them singing,
Taught them sung prayers; dug clay; would not talk;
The {{p|Carpathian}} hills; his secret's bringing

Came late, at thirty-six; a *baal shem*, he,
Master of the Name, healer, charms, the best;
They called him {{c|4017|Baal Shem Tov}}: the praise, the plea,
As {{c|4018|Master of the Good Name}}; and, at rest,

His home at {{p|Medzhybizh}}, near forty; law
He kept, but taught another heart: there's none,
No place empty of Him: the field, the straw,
The tavern, stranger, evil thought; each one;

Each spark the {{c|3985|Kabbalists}} had mourned, below,
In things, waits to be lifted up with joy,
Not fasting; joy; the sad are far; and so
The simple near; and this one, of the boy:

On {{c|3926|Yom Kippur}} a shepherd who can't read
Stood all day in the synagogue, his heart
Full, with a shepherd's pipe; and, at the need
Of closing prayer, he blew it; and the start

Of sound in that room made the men turn wild;
{{c|4017|Baal Shem Tov}}: "The gates of heaven were shut;
Our prayers could not unlock them; but the child,
His pipe, a wordless heart, broke them"; the rut

Of learning was no road; the heart, the road.
He wrote nothing; students wrote him: the great
{{c|4019|Maggid}} of {{p|Mezhyrichi}}; and the load
Of tales the poor passed on, and softened weight;

And like the water, spread through villages
{{c|4020|Hasidism}}: pious, dancing in prayer,
A rebbe's court, the feasting's images
Of song drew in the poor; and then, aware,

The {{c|4021|Vilna Gaon}}, the greatest scholar, came
{{p|Vilnius}}: excommunicated them
Seventy-two: "Dancers, not scholars"; same,
The quarrel cooled in time; both held the hem

Of the {{c|2500|Jews}} of the East, {{x|Jewish}}, as one;
And here's the thing for this book: rebbes' courts
Grew dynasties: from father on to son,
The rebbe's coat held by heirs; and supports

Of holy kin, kept as with any king;
His great-grandson, {{c|4022|Nachman of Breslov}}, taught
The world's a narrow bridge, and the main thing
Is not to fear at all; and his grave's brought

To {{p|Uman}} thousands each new year, to pray;
Hold this: the holy is in each, and there
In families, too; the courts, the line, the way
Of rebbes' kin; and keep the shepherd's air:

The pipe's the part to keep; and this, which shares
The {{x|Gaiad}} with the {{c|4017|Baal Shem Tov}}: that none
Is empty; sacred life in all: the stairs,
The straw, the stranger, smallest thing, each one;

The plenty in all things; lift it with joy;
The sad are far from sacred; sing to school;
No words? Then blow the whistle, like the boy;
What you had was enough; the heart, the rule.


# Chapter 284: The Pact at Diriyah

{{p|Najd}}, the high heart of {{p|Arabia}}, there,
From {{p|Istanbul}} and {{p|Cairo}}, palm and clay,
Where people hung rags on trees, asked the prayer
Of saints; and one, severe, came home one day,

The scholar {{c|4023|al-Wahhab}}, the one who taught,
Home from {{p|Medina}}, {{p|Basra}}: "This is not
{{x|Islam}}. For God is one; no saint is sought,
No tree, no tomb, no prophet, may be got

To intercede." He reached back past the time,
The {{c|3957|Sufi}} orders, shrines, saints' feasts, the schools
Of law and commentaries, to the prime
Beginning, as he read it; and his rules,

*{{x|The Oneness of God}}*, simple, absolute;
At {{p|Al-Uyaynah}}, with its emir, he
Cut down a sacred tree; tore, at the root,
The tomb of {{c|4024|Zayd ibn al-Khattab}}; he

Had a woman stoned. The town grew afraid;
The emir's lord sent him away; he went
To {{p|Diriyah}}, dry riverbed, and made
In forty-four, with its emir, content:

{{c|4025|Muhammad ibn Saud}}; the preacher said:
"Your sword and your protection; I, the creed,
And right to rule in it." The {{c|4026|Saud}} were wed
To land; the {{c|4027|Al ash-Sheikh}}, the rite, indeed;

Two dynasties in one hand, married through
Each generation, to this day; and hold
This, in a book of kin: two trees that grew,
Bound by a promise in a mud-brick fold

Of conquest: {{c|4028|Al-Muwahhidun}}, as one
God's oneness; and their foes' name for them stuck:
*{{x|Wahhabi}}*. They took {{p|Najd}}, and further won;
North to {{p|Karbala}}, in {{p|Iraq}}; and struck

The holy city of the {{c|2775|Shia}}, where
{{c|4029|Husayn}}, the {{c|2776|Prophet}}'s grandson, died; they killed
Thousands, stripped the shrine; took {{p|Mecca}}, and, there,
{{p|Medina}}; {{p|Baqi}}'s domes, the kin's, they spilled

To ground; the pilgrims of another way
Turned back. {{c|3115|Ottomans}} sent {{x|Egyptian}} might,
Seven years; in eighteen-eighteen, razed lay
{{p|Diriyah}}; {{c|4031|Abdullah}} beheaded; night.

The realm won; the idea had not; kept
In desert, it returned; and, by the sword,
Young {{c|4032|Ibn Saud}} retook {{p|Riyadh}}; and, swept,
{{p|Baqi}}'s domes fell again; the oil outpoured

Beneath the sands; the kingdom of his name
Stands, and the preaching, quiet, loud, goes forth
With oil's wealth; still the pact, the two, the same
Families, sheikh and emir, south and north,

To mosques and schools across the world. Now hold
This close: it is the spine of this whole book.
The fight was over graves: who may enfold
The dead in a dome, who may come and look.

The domes at {{p|Baqi}} kept the {{c|2776|Prophet}}'s kin;
The preacher said no grave should stand between;
A rag on a tree let the widow in.
The one God and the asker; keep it clean.

So the dispute was ours, the oldest one:
Who may honour which dead, and by whose leave;
The sheikh's house and the sword, or everyone
Who brought a rag to the saint's tomb, to grieve.

A faith, a state, two family trees, one pact:
That is a thing this book can honour whole;
The house of the sheikh holds the rite, intact,
The emir's house the land: one house, one soul.

What the sword cut away was ours as well:
The {{c|3957|Sufi}} lodges, saints' feasts, and the shrine
Where {{c|2764|Muslims}}, {{c|2494|Christians}}, {{c|2500|Jews}} would kneel and tell
Their prayers side by side, as kin of one line.

Hold the tree they cut down. Its shade was free;
The one who prayed beneath it is our own.
God is one, the preacher said; so are we:
One house, with room for rag and dome and stone.


# Chapter 285: The Assessor of the Board of Mines

His father, {{c|4033|Jesper Swedberg}}, {{p|Skara}}'s head
As bishop, saw the angels, talked with them;
Ennobled, seventeen-nineteen; instead
Of Swedberg, {{c|4034|Swedenborg}}; a name, a stem

Made new, as the linden named {{c|4012|Linnaeus}}' line;
The son, {{c|4035|Emanuel}}, in {{p|Stockholm}} born,
Sixteen eighty-eight, practical and fine,
Sat thirty years on the {{c|4036|Board of Mines}}, sworn

To copper, iron, safety in the shafts,
The kingdom's wealth; a scientist of all:
A flying machine, fixed-wing, paper drafts,
The brain: the cortex held the mind, its wall

Of parts, each part its own; the planets, spun
From a cloud round the sun; learned {{x|Hebrew}}; famed;
At fifty-five, in forty-three, begun,
Dreams; and the granite cracked; kept, unashamed,

A journal, tender, of a man undone:
Temptations, terrors, {{c|1497|Christ}} appearing; and,
In April forty-five, in {{p|London}}, one
Inn, after dinner, came a man, at hand:

"Do not eat so much"; and that night, the Lord
Appeared, and gave a task: to open wide
The inner meaning of the scripture stored;
He gave up science, all but that; and plied

Thirty years' books in {{x|Latin}}, nameless, sent
From {{p|London}}: *{{x|Heavenly Secrets}}*, in eight,
On {{c|4037|Genesis}} and {{c|4038|Exodus}}; he went,
*{{x|Heaven and Hell}}*; he walked the spirit's state

Each day, as down a street, and with the dead
He talked: that heaven is a state of love,
Not a reward; the angels, men, instead;
That married love goes on; and that the dove,

The light, the water, tree: each natural thing
Corresponds to a spirit one; the day
{{x|Last Judgment}} came in fifty-seven: ring
In spirit world, unseen on earth; the way

In fifty-nine, at {{p|Gothenburg}}, he dined,
Four hundred kilometres off; turned pale,
Went out, came back: "{{p|Stockholm}} burns"; and, behind,
Hour after hour, he told the guests the tale;

At eight: "Thank {{c|472|God}}, it stopped, three doors away
From mine"; the courier, days on, said so;
It was; and {{c|4039|Kant}} at {{p|Königsberg}}, the way
Mocked it in *{{x|Dreams of a Spirit-Seer}}*; though

He could not let it go. Hold, whole, the man,
As {{c|3896|Bureus}}, {{c|3895|Newton}}: mines, brain, and the sun
Cloud, and the visions; like {{c|3895|Newton}}, one plan,
Seer, scientist, one button, pressed: and done,

"I've seen; believe or not." He did not ask
For a church. Dying in {{p|London}}, he knew:
When {{c|4040|John Wesley}} wrote to meet him, his task
Was answered: "I die March twenty-ninth"; true,

He died that day. His readers made, and kept,
The {{c|4041|New Church}}; and his seeds became the trees
Of orchards where his readers' footsteps stepped;
The {{x|Gaiad}} says: here's one who's sure, who sees

The other world, which planted trees in him;
Each natural thing corresponds: the tree,
The water, the pure light; plant, at the rim,
The tree; and leave the page; walk barefoot, free,

With seeds, in a strange country; and the yield
Is for those you won't meet. His bones lie, home,
In {{p|Uppsala}}'s church, near {{c|4012|Linnaeus}}, sealed;
The farthest visions, nearest names: one dome.


# Chapter 286: All Knowledge in One Structure

It started as a job; {{c|4048|Le Breton}} planned
{{c|4049|Chambers}}' *{{x|Cyclopaedia}}* into {{x|French}},
Hired a cutler's son, {{p|Langres}}', in hand,
{{c|4050|Denis Diderot}} and {{c|4051|d'Alembert}}; the wrench:

They would not translate; they would make it new:
A dictionary, reasoned, of all things,
The sciences, arts, crafts, to change, all through,
The common way of thinking; prison's stings

Already, {{p|Vincennes}}: three months, a line
The blind that doubted God; he knew the risk.
First volume, fifty-one; the chart, the sign,
A tree of human knowledge, branches brisk:

From {{c|4053|Francis Bacon}}: Memory, which grows
History; Reason, philosophy; arts
Imagination; God, a twig, there shows
On Reason's branch, filed with the mind's own parts

Of world and heaven in one human scheme;
The quarrel was who files the tree. The words:
Seventy-two thousand entries; a team
Of writers: {{c|4001|Voltaire}}, {{c|4054|Rousseau}}, and the herds

Of the forgotten; {{c|4055|de Jaucourt}}, one, sure,
Wrote seventeen thousand, unpaid, and paid
Secretaries, himself; his name kept pure:
Plain labour; and subversion, slyly laid

In dull entries: cannibals, at the end:
*See: {{x|Eucharist}}*: a jab from kin at kin.
The plates: eleven volumes, made to send
Of workshops, not kings: how to step within

The forge, the loom, the press, the mine, the frame
Of stockings, glass and pins: tool and motion;
Hands' knowledge set beside the mind's, the same
In dignity: the whole book's devotion:

The artisan, philosopher of craft.
Banned, of course: the king's council, fifty-two;
Fifty-nine, privilege revoked, the draft
Illegal, {{c|2825|Pope}} condemning; turned on two

Men: the chief censor, of all men, himself,
{{c|4056|Malesherbes}}, who believed, warned him of the raid;
Hid manuscripts in his own house, his shelf,
Where the police would not look; and, afraid,

The publisher, {{c|4048|Le Breton}}, took the proofs
Of the last ten, cut each dangerous line;
And {{c|4052|Diderot}} found out, sixty-four; the roofs
Of his life fell; years' work and the design,

Cut by the man who'd paid; he wept with rage;
He finished; the last plates, seventy-two;
And, needing his daughter's dowry, the sage
Sold {{c|3695|Catherine}} of {{p|Russia}} books; she knew

Their worth; he kept them, paid as their keeper;
Hold the whole of it, as this book has learned:
Register to free the mind, and deeper;
The Bacon tree, God under reason turned;

The hands, the crafts, honoured; the censor, brave;
The publisher who cut. And still the dream:
Now, anyone can edit; and the wave
Of many hands makes the largest, a stream

{{c|3880|Ophiuchus}} tells; give thanks: twig and tree,
To {{c|4057|Jaucourt}}'s seventeen thousand; the plate
Of the weaver's lever: many hands, free;
Write knowledge down, and make it free, and great.


# Chapter 287: The Bard Who Never Was

In forty-six, {{p|Culloden}}'s moor: there broke
The last {{x|Jacobite}} host; the realm, to stay,
Unmade the {{p|Scottish Highlands}}: clans, the yoke
On chiefs; the tartan, kilt, and plaid's display

Banned for thirty-five years; the {{c|4058|Gaelic}} world
Was being cleared; in sixty, from that land,
{{c|4059|James Macpherson}}, a tutor, young, unfurled
In {{p|Edinburgh}} a small book, at hand:

*{{x|Fragments of Ancient Poetry}}*, the voice
Of {{c|4060|Ossian}}, blind bard of ages gone,
Son of {{c|4061|Fingal}}, sang {{c|4062|Oscar}}, dead; his choice
Of mist, ghosts on the wind, the grey sea's dawn,

The moon, the fallen, and the harp. The stir
Was instant: gentlemen paid him to go
Up to the {{p|Highlands}}, more, the {{c|4058|Gaelic}} burr;
He brought back *{{c|4061|Fingal}}*, sixty-one; and so

*{{x|Temora}}*: {{c|4063|Homer of the North}}, in sight,
The islands' {{x|Iliad}}; and {{p|Europe}} wept;
{{x|Romantic}} age rose on those pages' light;
{{c|4064|Goethe}}'s young {{c|4065|Werther}} read him, before he stepped

Into his death, aloud, to her he loved;
And {{p|Sweden}}'s kings, today, bear {{c|4062|Oscar}}'s name,
Born of the bard's son; and his, beloved,
{{c|4069|Selma}}, {{c|4061|Fingal}}'s hall, a girl's name, the same:

{{c|4070|Selma Lagerlöf}} bore it; and, as one,
{{c|3593|Jefferson}} called him greatest ever; and
Then {{c|4073|Samuel Johnson}}, in {{p|London}}, as one
Who doubted, asked for manuscripts in hand;

{{c|4072|Macpherson}} had them in the glens: the songs
Of old {{x|Fenian}} tales still sung, alive;
From them he made the whole; and so belongs
